title: Residual bucket: one-off meter and deal fixes in gas logistics

narrative.what_happens: These messages sit in a single logistics mailbox folder and each one raises or passes along a problem with a meter or a deal — a meter overflow, a counterparty deal that needs looking at, a deal that needs correcting. Every message was classified as informational (fyi) rather than as a request, an escalation or a correction, and each belongs to its own separate thread, so no follow-up traffic is visible inside the cluster. The activity phrases the earlier pass extracted are generic ("resolve deal issue", "resolve meter or deal issue") and no shared artefact, system or distribution list appears across them beyond plain email. What the output of each item was, and who closed it, is not visible in the evidence given here. Read as one process this is a residual grouping of unrelated one-off fixes rather than a repeating procedure.
narrative.where_it_stalls: No stall is observable. The measured rework, waiting, manual-transfer and deadline rates are all zero, every role is fyi, and each of the nine messages is a distinct single-message thread, so there is no evidence of chasing, re-doing work, or a cutoff being missed. Any failure mode asserted here would be invented rather than found.
narrative.why_it_recurs: Meter and deal problems arise continuously in gas logistics, so a catch-all phrase like "resolve deal issue" collects scattered one-off items across many months. The grouping recurs as a label, not as a repeating procedure.
narrative.automation_opportunity: Nothing in this cluster is specific enough to automate. The only reasonable mechanism is upstream: route meter and deal exceptions into a tracked queue with a reason code, so future items of this kind carry enough structure to be grouped by cause instead of falling into an unclassified bucket.

steps: 9.00 task instances / 6 months of coverage = 1.500 instances per month
minutes per instance = 6 handle + (1.00 touches - 1) x 3 + 0.00 rework rate x 6 + 0.00 waiting rate x 2 = 6.00 min
